einzeiler: Paleontologist Kenneth Lacovara discusses dinosaurs, fossils, and the history of Earth.
kurzfassung: Paleontologist Kenneth Lacovara joins the podcast to discuss the reality of dinosaurs, the history of the fossil record, and how ancient life can be understood through modern science. He explains the massive scale of prehistoric creatures, the mechanics of fossilization, and the events surrounding their extinction. The conversation also explores geological history, famous discoveries, and the ongoing work at the Edelman Fossil Park and Museum.
stichpunkte: Discussion on dinosaur skepticism and the overwhelming physical evidence of their existence.
Mapping Earth's history onto a calendar year, showing dinosaurs arriving in December and going extinct after Christmas.
The rarity of fossilization and why most individual creatures never enter the fossil record.
The history of early dinosaur discoveries, including Megalosaurus and Hadrosaurus.
Debates surrounding feathers on dinosaurs and how modern birds connect directly to theropods.
The discovery and massive size of Dreadnoughtus in South America.
The mechanics of the asteroid impact 66 million years ago and how certain burrowing animals survived.
The history of geology, magnetic pole shifts, and the contributions of scientists like Nicholas Steno and James Hutton.

clips.hook: Mapping Earth's history onto a single calendar year
clips.text: If the four-and-a-half-billion-year history of the planet is compressed into a single year, complex life only appears around Thanksgiving, dinosaurs arrive in December, and humans emerge just moments before midnight on New Year's Eve.

clips.hook: The double standard of bringing back extinct animals
clips.text: Society readily embraces projects aimed at resurrecting mammoths or dire wolves while viewing the potential recreation of a Neanderthal as an ethical boundary that should not be crossed.

clips.hook: A terrifying moment clinging to a cliff face
clips.text: While carrying a heavy slab of rock containing flying reptile tracks up a steep outcrop, the handholds began crumbling away, leaving the climber stranded without a clear way down.

beschreibung:
Kenneth Lacovara, PhD, is a paleontologist, founding dean of the School of Earth & Environment at Rowan University, and director of the Jean & Ric Edelman Fossil Park. He is the author of "Why Dinosaurs Matter."
